topic: A teacher receives an unexpected gift from a former student
text: The envelope arrives, heavier than air, settling on my desk like a bird that’s flown too far. I recognize the handwriting, a script from the past, a student's grace. My fingers hesitate, as if the paper might speak if handled too roughly. Inside, a card, delicate as the subject I taught, crisp with genuine thanks and, tucked within, a small token. A book, older than the years I've spent here, yet it bears a fresh inscription. Each word a step back in time, each page a memory warmed by sunlight through classroom windows. My hands form a cradle, holding not just an object, but seasons of lessons and laughter, now offered back to me.
